summary: When/how the saltern MAGs were assembled and binned, what tools have improved since, and whether re-assembly/re-binning is worth it

provenance.summary:
The cores were sampled in July 2014 (R1, R2 and R2A on 2014-07-11; SF2 on 2014-07-17); the three R2_restored samples were collected on 2015-03-10. JGI sequenced all 39 libraries under proposal 1890 (approved 2015-03-02, PI Tringe) on two Illumina HiSeq 2500 runs: run 10057 (18 libraries, Dec 2015) and run 10092 (21 libraries, Jan 2016). Each library is one 2x151 bp run. The raw reads are public in SRA/ENA: 39 runs, 344.10 Gbp.

Each sample has up to three different assemblies:
- **(i) JGI standard assembly.** MEGAHIT v1.0.3 per Zhou et al., made 2015-12-26 to 2016-01-12 and annotated in IMG in 2016 (IMG 3300007532 to 3300009145). It exists for 38 samples (none for R1_C_H2O). This is the source of the IMG KO profiles and is what the manuscript's Metagenomics paragraph describes.
- **(ii) JGI IMG-team "SPAdes version 2" reassembly.** Made 2018-03-21 to 2018-04-17 (IMG 3300026094 to 3300026251). Its IMG submission IDs 185694 to 185731 are exactly the /scratch/chenry/.../metagenome_assemblies files used by the Henry-lab CoverM runs.
- **(iii) The Tringe lab's own per-sample reassembly.** BBTools Tadpole error correction plus SPAdes (Zhou 2022), SPAdes version not reported. This is the true source of the 450 MAG contigs.

I tested (iii) against (ii) directly. None of 129,258 MAG contigs in 33 samples matches the v2 reassembly by NODE index and length, and only 1.6% of contigs of 20 kb or more have their length anywhere in it. The MAG-source assemblies have about 2-8x more contigs of 2.5 kb or more. R1_C_H2O has no JGI assembly at all, yet has 6 MAGs. The (iii) assemblies are not in IMG, NCBI or KBase.

The MAGs were binned on each per-sample assembly (contigs of 2.5 kb or more) with CONCOCT, MaxBin and MetaBAT, refined with DAS Tool, then checked with CheckM (completeness >70%, contamination <25%). dRep (gANI >96.5%, 60% overlap) kept 310 and set aside 140. All 450 come from 39 metagenomes, not 24: of the 310, 209 come from the 24 cores, 64 from the 12 water samples and 37 from the 3 R2_restored samples.

Binning date is bounded by BBTools "accessed 16 April 2018" (Genes 2021) and the KBase upload on 2020-11-18. Most tool versions for the MAG pipeline are unreported. The only ones named are CheckM 1.0.18 and GTDB-Tk 1.1.0, in the Marivita paper.

For the user's question: the MAG-source assemblies are not public and the whole pipeline dates from 2015-2018, so any reassessment would reassemble from the 344 Gbp of public raw reads. In SF2 and R2A sediments only 5-34% of reads map even to the whole JGI v2 assembly (contigs of 500 bp or more). That suggests sequencing depth and assembly, not just the binning tools, limit the binned fraction there (inference).

discrepancies: MEGAHIT vs SPAdes. Manuscript paragraph 30 (Metabolic Manuscript.docx, python-docx index): 'The 24 metagenomes were quality filtered and trimmed with BBtools, assembled with MEGAHIT'. Paragraph 35: MAGs 'were assembled from the 24 metagenomes'. MEGAHIT v1.0.3 is right only for JGI's standard IMG assemblies, which supplied the KO profiles. The MAGs come from separate per-sample Tadpole+SPAdes re-assemblies (Zhou PMC8692437.txt line 23), which is why all 145,616 MAG contigs carry SPAdes NODE_ headers (MAG_contigs/README.md line 26). The Methods need one sentence for the IMG/KO assemblies and another for the MAG assemblies.

The MAG source is neither IMG assembly. Genes 2021 (PMC8535929.txt line 15) cites 'IMG ID 3300026157' (the JGI 2018 '(SPAdes) (version 2)' record) for the Methanosalis MAG. Yet 0/129,258 MAG contigs match that reassembly's contigs by index and length (node_vs_img.tsv), and only 1.6% of contigs of 20 kb or more have their length in it (node_rank.tsv). So IMG IDs in the papers identify the sample, not the assembly that was binned. The MAG-source assemblies are not deposited anywhere I checked (IMG, NCBI 'Salt_Pond_MetaG' search = 0 hits, KBase). R1_C_H2O has no JGI assembly at all (Zhou Table S1 IMG ID 'NA') yet contributes 6 MAGs.

24 vs 39 metagenomes. The MAGs were binned from 39 metagenomes (Zhou Table S1 lists 39: 26 'Sediment' incl. 2 R2_restored, 13 'Water'). The 310 retained MAGs split 209 from the 24 cores, 64 from the 12 water samples and 37 from the 3 R2_restored samples (all 450: 313/96/41). Abundance and unbinned fractions were computed only on the 24 cores (Cliff_310MAG_relabund.tsv has 24 core columns; Genes papers: 'across the 24 metagenome samples'). 'Assembled from the 24 metagenomes' is wrong for binning but right for quantification.

Sampling date. The 3 R2_restored samples were collected 2015-03-10 (SRA collection_date), not in July 2014. SF2 was sampled 2014-07-17 and R1/R2/R2A on 2014-07-11. Manuscript paragraph 27 ('July, 2014') holds only for the 24 cores, but 37 of the 310 MAGs come from the 2015 samples.

Sequencing yield. Zhou line 21 says '~20 Gb ... for each metagenome sample ... for a total of 700 Gb with ~400 bp inserts'. SRA/ENA show 6.14-12.44 Gbp per run and 344.10 Gbp over the 39 runs, with nominal_length 270 for every library. Genes 2021 ('Approximately 10 Gb' for R1_A_D2) matches SRA (8.92 Gbp). Zhou's figures are about 2x high.

Unbinned fractions disagree within the manuscript. Paragraph 96 gives '88% in SF2, 89% in R2A, 58% in R2, and 47% in R1', which matches Cliff's table (means 0.884/0.891/0.580/0.469). The Table 3 caption (paragraph 113) gives '68%, 89%, and 89%' for unrestored/restored/reference, but the unrestored mean from the same table is ~52%.

IMG annotation pipeline 'v4.10.2' (paragraph 30) is UNVERIFIED. The per-sample pipeline_version.info (2016-03-02) sits behind a JGI login and is purged to tape. A 2016 MAP v4-era pipeline is consistent, but the exact version is not confirmed.

CheckM numbers in Zhou disagree slightly with themselves. Zhou states contamination <25%, but Table S2 has a maximum of 25.53%. The text gives 'contamination from 12 to 24%' for the 35 contaminated MAGs; Table S2 shows 10.16-25.53%. Separately, the local KBase reduced-tree CheckM 1.0.18 table matches Zhou S2 for 301/310 MAGs but puts one MAG below 70% completeness (63.27%), while Zhou S2's minimum is 75.44%.

Zhou Table S1 mixes measures in 'Assembled Genome Size'. For the 24 cores it reports IMG total bases including unassembled reads (R1_A_D1 1,426,804,145 = JGI portal img.total_bases; the assembled size is 689,817,367 in IMG_Info.xlsx). For the water and R2_restored rows it reports assembled size.

Citation issues. Zhou ref 39 and Genes 2021 ref 35 cite Lin & Liao 2016 (MyCC) for CONCOCT; CONCOCT's paper is Alneberg et al. 2014. The manuscript text has 'Zhou et al. (202)' typos (paragraphs 27-28) and 'Zhou et al. (2021)' for a paper whose reference is ISME J 16:284-295 (online 2021-07-28, issue Jan 2022). The reference list also omits co-author Ye Tian.

advances.summary: WHEN (verified from Zhou et al. 2022 Methods, PMC8692437, plus release dates): the JGI/IMG assemblies were made with MEGAHIT v1.0.3 (a 2015-10-11 release). The MAGs come from a separate per-sample re-assembly ('Tadpole error correction in BBTools and the SPAdes assembler'; SPAdes version and whether --meta was used are not reported). Each assembly was binned with CONCOCT, MaxBin and MetaBAT, merged by DAS Tool (2018 paper), scored with CheckM, and dereplicated with dRep (gANI >96.5%, 60% overlap). So this is a 2018-2020 pipeline: the FASTAs reached KBase on 2020-11-18 (KBase provenance in the user's MAG-inventory notes), and the paper was received 2021-01-19 and published online 2021-07-28. The manuscript's 'assembled with MEGAHIT' describes the IMG assemblies, not the MAG assemblies. Locally, 112 of 1,287 R2A_B_D1 MAG contigs are longer than that sample's longest IMG contig (16,025 bp). WHAT CHANGED SINCE: (1) Short-read assemblers have not improved much. CAMI II found 'performances were similar across software versions'. SPAdes 3.14-4.3 releases are about speed and RAM, and v4.0 was declared the last major feature release. MEGAHIT has had no release since 1.2.9 (2019). (2) Binning has improved. Multi-sample (differential-coverage) binning gave +78% filtered bins and cut the share of bins with >=5% contamination from 22.5% to 3.5% (Mattock & Watson 2023, MetaBAT2 2.15). An independent 13-tool benchmark (Han 2025) found +100% MQ and +194% NC MAGs with 30 marine short-read samples, and its top-ranked short-read binner is COMEBin. In the tools' own papers, the newer binners (COMEBin, SemiBin/SemiBin2, MetaBinner, MetaDecoder, VAMB/AVAMB/TaxVAMB) recover about 10-80% more near-complete or HQ genomes than MetaBAT2 or a CONCOCT/MaxBin/MetaBAT + DAS Tool ensemble (2-3x in some datasets). Newer refiners such as MAGScoT add only about 5-25% over DAS Tool. (3) Quality estimation has improved. For poorly represented or reduced-genome phyla, including Nanohaloarchaeota, CheckM2's completeness error is 3.6% vs 26.3% for CheckM1. GUNC flags 15-30% of 'HQ' MAGs in large studies as chimeras. skani-based dereplication (dRep v4, galah) removes the low-ANI bias that Mash/FastANI show on incomplete MAGs. VERDICT: re-QC is clearly worth doing (CheckM2 + GUNC + skani, no re-assembly needed). Re-binning with all-vs-all coverage across the 39 samples, a ~1 kb contig floor, a modern binner and a refiner is probably worthwhile: expect more and cleaner MAGs, mainly from the unrestored cores and the water samples. Re-assembling only to get a newer assembler version is not worthwhile. In the SF2/R2A cores the ~88% of reads that are unbinned are mostly unassembled: only ~14-15% of their reads map to >=500 bp contigs of the IMG assembly, and the MAGs already hold 9-12%. No binner can fix that; it needs deeper or long-read sequencing, or per-site co-assembly.

advances.relevance_here: Local measurements come from the existing CoverM 0.7.0/strobealign runs in /home/freiburger/Documents/MicrobiomeNotebooks/salterns/reads/coverm/*/coverm_metagenome.out, coverm_bins.out and BAM headers. They are tabulated in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-freiburger-Documents-MicrobiomeNotebooks-salterns/a24fbb2e-9d33-5e05-aeea-a07d777ccde7/scratchpad/rebinning/assembly_vs_bins.tsv. (1) ASSEMBLY, NOT BINNING, LIMITS THE RESTORED/REFERENCE CORES. In the 6 R2A cores, a mean 15.1% of reads map to the sample's own IMG MEGAHIT assembly (contigs >=500 bp), and the 450 MAGs recruit 9.3%. In SF2 cores the figures are 14.2% vs 12.0%. In the unrestored cores the MAGs already hold 94-97% of the assembled reads (R1 53.9% vs 52.3%; R2 41.4% vs 38.9%). So ~85% of SF2/R2A core reads never assembled into >=500 bp contigs. Even a perfect re-binning of that assembly could add only ~2-6 percentage points of reads. Caveats: the MAGs were binned from a separate SPAdes re-assembly that is more contiguous (in R2A_B_D1, 112 of 1,287 MAG contigs are longer than the longest IMG contig, 16,025 bp), and its read recruitment is unmeasured. MAG recruitment is competitive mapping against MAGs from all 39 samples. 6 of the 39 samples lack the IMG-assembly BAM. Getting these cores well above ~11-12% binned needs more depth, long reads, or per-site co-assembly of the 6 replicate cores, not a new binner. Sereika et al. 2025 report 183% more dereplicated MAGs from 154 deeply Nanopore-sequenced soils/sediments than from ~10,700 shallow short-read samples (PMC12313526). CAMI II supports co-assembly for low-coverage genomes without cross-sample strain diversity. (2) THE 2.5 KB FLOOR IS THE BEST-QUANTIFIED LEVER. All 145,616 MAG contigs are >=2,500 bp. In the IMG assemblies only ~20% (R2A cores) and ~23% (SF2 cores) of assembled bp lie in contigs >=2.5 kb, vs 41% (R1) and 34% (R2). CAMI II links a drop in mean completeness from 36.9% to 21.2% to unbinned 1.5-2 kb contigs. Binning >=1 kb contigs with 39-sample coverage (COMEBin default; MetaBAT2 --minContigByCorr 1000; SemiBin2 --min-len set explicitly, because its automatic drop to 1 kb triggers only when 1-2.5 kb contigs hold <5% of bp; this rule is from the SemiBin1 paper, so confirm it in the SemiBin2 docs) should mostly raise completeness of existing MAGs and add some new ones, at some cost in purity. (3) MULTI-SAMPLE COVERAGE IS THE LARGEST DOCUMENTED GAIN, BUT IT SCALES WITH SHARED SAMPLES. The documented gains are +78% filtered bins with contaminated bins cut from 22.5% to 3.5% (Mattock & Watson), and +100% MQ / +194% NC with 30 marine samples, but only +22% MQ and comparable NC/HQ with 3 samples (Han 2025). The 39 samples here are 4 sites x (6 cores + 3 waters) plus 3 extra R2 samples, so a given taxon probably co-occurs in ~6-12 samples. Expect a gain between those two extremes (extrapolation, not measured). Zhou et al.'s 'read depths across samples' may mean cross-sample coverage was already used (unverified), in which case part of this gain is already realised. (4) WHERE RE-BINNING SHOULD PAY OFF. In the unrestored cores (16-20 MAGs per sample; most assembled reads already binned), gains would be more NC/HQ MAGs, fewer chimeras, and strain separation within the 25 Rhodobacteraceae (12 Roseovarius). Among the 35 MAGs with CheckM contamination >=10%, multi-coverage binning is the documented fix. The water samples have the most headroom: the assembly recruits 38-93% of reads, but MAGs hold only 23-68% of that (SF2 H2O 38.0% vs 8.7%) and they yield 5-9 MAGs per sample vs 16-20 in R1/R2 cores. These samples are therefore limited by binning and retention; plausible causes are brine strain microdiversity, eukaryotic or viral DNA, and the >70% completeness retention cutoff (unverified). (5) NOVEL HYPERSALINE LINEAGES FAVOUR REFERENCE-FREE BINNERS. At GTDB r232, 134 of 310 MAGs lack a species name and 20 lack a genus. There are 30 archaea (24 Halobacteriota, 3 Nanohalarchaeota, 2 Thermoproteota, 1 Asgardarchaeota) and 15 Bacillota (MAG_QC/gtdbtk_local_r232/*.summary.tsv). TaxVAMB, SemiBin1 and GUNC depend on reference taxonomy; in CAMI II, Nanohaloarchaeota were 'not detected at all' by taxonomic profilers. SemiBin2 has no hypersaline pretrained model. So the best choices here are self-trained SemiBin2, COMEBin, VAMB and MetaBAT2, combined with MAGScoT or Binette. (6) RE-QC IS CHEAP AND NEEDS NO RE-ASSEMBLY. 106 of 310 MAGs were scored by CheckM1 with only domain-level markers (99 k__Bacteria, 7 k__Archaea; MAG_QC/comparison_vs_2020.csv), the situation CheckM2's authors describe as 'reduced accuracy and sensitivity'. These include the 3 Nanohalarchaeota and 2 Patescibacteriota MAGs (CheckM1 completeness 63-85%), exactly the lineages where CheckM2 cut completeness error from 26.3% to 3.6%. Run CheckM2 and GUNC (plus multi-coverage correlation checks) on all 450 MAGs. Re-dereplicate with skani (dRep v4 or galah): Mash-based clustering under-estimates ANI for incomplete MAGs, so the 310/140 split may be slightly over-split (hypothesis). (7) PRACTICAL POINTS AND BOTTOM LINE. The per-sample SPAdes assemblies were not found locally or in KBase, where only binned contigs were uploaded (per the user's MAG inventory notes; existence elsewhere, e.g. at JGI, unverified). Re-binning may therefore require re-assembly anyway; if so, use metaSPAdes 4.x or MEGAHIT 1.2.9, but expect no accuracy gain from the version itself. Multi-sample coverage costs either 39 mappings to one concatenated reference (VAMB/SemiBin multi-split: "we first concatenate contigs from every sample into a single database to which short reads are mapped") or 39x39 = 1,521 pairwise mappings (Mattock/Han approach), with 39-78 M reads per library per the CoverM logs. Bottom line: re-QC, yes. Re-binning with multi-sample coverage, a >=1 kb floor, modern binner(s) and a refiner is likely worthwhile, giving more and cleaner MAGs mainly in the R1/R2 cores and water samples but only a modest change in the SF2/R2A binned fraction. Re-assembling only for a newer software version, no.
caveats: Nearly all quantitative gains come from simulated CAMI data or from human-gut, marine, rumen and soil datasets, mostly in the tool authors' own papers, against the 'second-best' tool. The only independent multi-tool real-data benchmark used here is Han et al. 2025, which used MEGAHIT 1.2.9 and CheckM2. No benchmark is hypersaline; the nearest is BASALT's Aiding Lake saline sediment, compared against metaWRAP and including gap-filling.

The local assembly-vs-MAG recruitment figures are against the IMG MEGAHIT assemblies (contigs >=500 bp), not the SPAdes re-assembly the MAGs were binned from. 6 of 39 samples (R1_C_D1, R1_C_H2O, R2_A_D2, R2_A_H2O, R2_C_D2, SF2_A_D1) have no IMG-assembly BAM. MAG recruitment is competitive mapping across all 450 MAGs, so it can exceed a sample's own assembly recruitment.

Whether the original binning used cross-sample (differential) coverage is unverified. Zhou et al. say reads were 'mapped to all contigs ... to get read depths across samples' but also that binning 'was performed on each individual assembly'.

The versions of SPAdes (and whether --meta was used), CONCOCT, MaxBin and MetaBAT are not reported. Zhou et al. cite the MetaBAT 1 (2015) and MaxBin 1 (2014) papers, and their reference 39 for CONCOCT is actually the MyCC paper.

CAMI II's 'assembler performances rose by up to 30%' vs CAMI 1 refers to HipMer/A-STAR-type gains (e.g., 30% fewer mismatches than Ray Meta). It is not evidence that MEGAHIT or metaSPAdes upgrades improve MAGs.

TaxVAMB numbers are from the 2026 Nat Biotechnol abstract (PMID 42045408); the 2024 preprint gave 40%/255%. The full text was not read. The CheckM2 numbers come from the published PDF hosted on NSF PAR. VAMB, CheckM2 (abstract) and Mattock & Watson are paywalled; quotes are from the PubMed abstracts and the Edinburgh accepted manuscript.

Binette: no quantitative benchmark in its JOSS paper; the bioRxiv preprint could not be read because of bioRxiv rate-limiting/Cloudflare, so its claimed gains are unverified. BinSPreader's and MetaCoAG's gains are not quantified here (MetaCoAG figures are from a 2021 preprint).

The 'expected gain' statements for this dataset (sample co-occurrence of ~6-12, the size of the 1-2.5 kb contig gain, possible over-splitting of the 310/140 dereplication) are extrapolations, not measurements. Causes of the water-sample binning gap (strain microdiversity, eukaryotic/viral DNA, the 70% completeness retention cutoff) are hypotheses.

The KBase CheckM 1.0.18 (reduced tree) table includes one MAG at 63.27% completeness, below Zhou et al.'s stated >70% retention filter. The original CheckM run behind the 310 selection may therefore differ from the table now in hand.

Long-read and hybrid sequencing (Sereika et al. 2025; Han et al. 2025 hybrid results) would be the main route to raising the binned fraction in high-diversity sediments, but that is new sequencing, outside a re-processing decision.

feasibility.summary:
Your two questions, answered first.

(1) WHEN WERE THE MAGs MADE? Roughly between April 2018 and November 2020. Zhou et al. built them, but not from the IMG assemblies the manuscript describes.
- Sampling: cores were taken in July 2014. Zhou et al., ISME J 16:284, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8692437/ : 'Soil core samples were collected from each sampling site in July 2014.'
- Sequencing and SRA release: JGI sequenced on a HiSeq 2500, 2x151 bp. Release dates came from NCBI E-utilities runinfo for the 39 BioSamples in Zhou Table S1 (saved at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-freiburger-Documents-MicrobiomeNotebooks-salterns/a24fbb2e-9d33-5e05-aeea-a07d777ccde7/scratchpad/rebinning/dl_sra/sra_runs_by_sample.csv): 23 runs on 2017-01-27, 4 on 2017-04-23, 6 on 2017-09-20, 1 on 2019-10-30 (R2_C_D2), and 5 on 2021-05-23 (R1_C_D1, R1_C_H2O, R2_A_D2, R2_A_H2O, SF2_A_D1).
- JGI assemblies, first round: MEGAHIT ('assembled using MEGAHIT v1.0.3.', PMC8692437). These are IMG 3300007xxx-3300009xxx, the KO-profile assemblies of manuscript paragraph 30.
- JGI assemblies, second round: JGI later added '(SPAdes) (version 2)' assemblies, IMG 33000260xx-33000262xx (salterns/exported_img_data.tsv, e.g. line 30 = 3300026156 R1_A_D1, line 55 = 3300026157 R1_A_D2). Not verified: the IMG and GOLD add-dates for either round. Both sites returned HTTP 403 or asked for a login. You can read the 'Add Date' off the IMG taxon page when logged in.
- The MAGs themselves come from Zhou et al.'s own re-assembly (PMC8692437):
  - 'Each metagenome was re-assembled (de novo) using Tadpole error correction in BBTools and the SPAdes assembler'
  - 'to generate longer contigs for high-quality bins.'
  - 'binning was performed on each individual assembly with three different tools (CONCOCT, MaxBin, and MetaBat)'
  - 'DAS Tool was used to select the best non-redundant set of genome bins from the three software tools'
  - Then CheckM and dRep.
- Dates that bracket the binning:
  - The companion Methanosalis paper (Genes 12:1609, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8535929) cites BBTools with an access date of 16 April 2018. This was paraphrased by the fetch tool and not checked against the page.
  - The 2020 GTDB table uses p__Halobacteriota (salterns/cliff_mags/gtdb_table_arc.csv line 2). That spelling first appears in GTDB R95: https://gtdb.ecogenomic.org/stats/r95 shows 'Halobacteriota 545' and 'GTDB release date: July 17, 2020', while R89 used 'Halobacterota 411' (https://gtdb.ecogenomic.org/stats/r89). So taxonomy was run on or after 17 July 2020.
  - The first object in KBase ws 77580 was saved 2020-11-18T06:16:01 (Workspace list_objects, today).
  - The paper was 'Received 2021 Jan 19'.
  - KBase CheckM 1.0.18 reproduces the 2020 CheckM table exactly (memory salterns-mag-inventory.md lines 71-73).
- Unexplained discrepancy, not an error: the paper says '~20 Gb' per sample and 700 Gb in total, but SRA holds 8.8 Gbp per sample and 344.1 Gbp in total.

(2) HAVE THE TOOLS ADVANCED ENOUGH TO JUSTIFY RE-DOING THIS? Binning and QC: yes. Assembly: barely.
- Assembly, from the GitHub release APIs today (saved at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-freiburger-Documents-MicrobiomeNotebooks-salterns/a24fbb2e-9d33-5e05-aeea-a07d777ccde7/scratchpad/rebinning/dl_github/latest_releases.json):
  - MEGAHIT's last release is still v1.2.9 (2019-10-15), the same version KBase runs.
  - SPAdes has gone from 3.x to v4.3.0 (2026-06-14).
- Binning:
  - Han et al. 2025, Nat Commun, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11933696/ : 'multi-sample binning achieves an average improvement of 125%, 54%, and 61%' (medium-quality, near-complete and high-quality MAG counts versus single-sample binning). Also: 'COMEBin achieved the highest overall ranking scores for hybrid_multi, hybrid_single, short_multi, and short_single'.
  - Mattock & Watson 2023, Nat Methods 20:1170, report 22.5% of single-coverage bins versus 3.5% of multi-coverage bins with contamination of 5 or more. This comes from a search snippet and was not checked against the paper.
  - Current versions: SemiBin 2.6.0, COMEBin 1.1.0, VAMB 5.0.4, DAS Tool 1.1.7, MetaBAT 2.18 (Bitbucket API, 2025-01-24).
- QC: CheckM2 1.1.0 and GUNC 1.1.1 exist; neither has been run on these MAGs.
- Zhou et al. may already have used depth across samples ('Metagenomic reads from each sample were mapped to all contigs using BBTools' and 'to get read depths across samples'). If so, multi-sample binning would gain less here.

NEW TEST 1: THE ASSEMBLIES ZHOU BINNED ARE NOT THE IMG ASSEMBLIES, AND WE CANNOT REACH THEM. Results are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-freiburger-Documents-MicrobiomeNotebooks-salterns/a24fbb2e-9d33-5e05-aeea-a07d777ccde7/scratchpad/rebinning/mag_vs_img_lengths.json.
- I compared exact contig lengths between the MAG contigs and the IMG SPAdes v2 assemblies, using the @SQ headers of the 2025 CoverM BAMs. The '.filtered' step on those files is undocumented; the shortest contig observed is 500 bp.
- Matches are at chance level in every length class. For R1_A_D1, contigs of 10-50 kb match 0.11 of the time, the same as a null with lengths shifted by 7 bp; contigs of 50 kb or more match 0 of 103.
- In 7 SF2/R2A sediment samples the MAGs contain more bp than the IMG assembly has in all its contigs of 2.5 kb or more (SF2_C_D1: 17.7 vs 8.6 Mb; R2A_B_D1: 9.8 vs 3.3 Mb).
- R1_C_H2O has 6 MAGs but no IMG assembly at all (Table S1 IMG ID is blank).
- Unresolved tension: the Genes 2021 paper names IMG 3300026157 as the metagenome the Methanosalis MAG came from ('The metagenome from which it was derived is also available with IMG ID 3300026157'). It may be citing the metagenome record rather than the exact assembly file.
- Where things stand: Zhou's per-sample SPAdes assemblies are not in IMG, not in KBase, and not on this machine. Locally we have only the 450 MAG contig sets (1.49 Gbp).

NEW TEST 2: IN THE RESTORED AND REFERENCE CORES, THE LIMIT IS ASSEMBLY, NOT BINNING. These numbers come from read-only passes over the 33 own-assembly BAMs on disk, plus the 2025 CoverM logs. Table: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-freiburger-Documents-MicrobiomeNotebooks-salterns/a24fbb2e-9d33-5e05-aeea-a07d777ccde7/scratchpad/rebinning/per_sample_summary.tsv.

Mean % of reads per site (sediment cores):

| Site | n | Map to own IMG v2 assembly | On contigs ≥1 kb | On contigs ≥2.5 kb | Recruited by the 310 MAGs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | 5 (R1_C_D1 absent) | 53.9 | 45.2 | 33.2 | 49.5 |
| R2 | 4 | 41.4 | 32.3 | 20.9 | 36.9 |
| R2A | 6 | 15.1 | 10.2 | 6.0 | 9.0 |
| SF2 | 5 | 14.2 | 10.0 | 5.4 | 11.2 |

The rest of what the MAGs capture comes from MAGs binned in other samples (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-freiburger-Documents-MicrobiomeNotebooks-salterns/a24fbb2e-9d33-5e05-aeea-a07d777ccde7/scratchpad/rebinning/own_vs_other.json).

INPUTS AVAILABLE

THIS MACHINE

feasibility.recommendation:
Short answer: re-assembling and re-binning is not worth it for this manuscript. Do the cheap, targeted fixes now, and treat any re-processing as a gated pilot or a follow-up study.

Why not now:
1. What has really advanced since the 2018-2020 binning is binning and QC (multi-sample coverage, SemiBin2/COMEBin, CheckM2/GUNC), not short-read assembly. MEGAHIT is still 1.2.9 from 2019.
2. The 88-89% unbinned in the SF2/R2A cores is an assembly ceiling, not a binning failure. Only 14-15% of their reads align to their own assembly and 5-6% lie on contigs of 2.5 kb or more (R2A n=6, SF2 n=5), while the current MAGs already recruit 9-11%. Re-binning cannot fix that.
3. The assemblies Zhou binned cannot be reached, and the IMG ones are measurably different (worse in SF2/R2A). So any re-bin produces a new MAG set. That means redoing abundances, guilds, correlations, 266 + 618 FBAModels, the curated betaine and MePn models, Tables 3 and S5, and Figures 7 and S11, and dropping 'MAGs of Zhou et al.'. Modelling on KBase was also unreliable at scale.

Do now:
1. Fix the Methods. The MAGs come from 39 metagenomes (24 cores, 12 water, 3 R2_restored), assembled with Tadpole + SPAdes per sample and binned with CONCOCT/MaxBin/MetaBat + DAS Tool + CheckM + dRep (Zhou et al.). MEGAHIT v1.0.3 and IMG pipeline v4.10.2 apply only to the KO-profile assemblies.
2. Run option (a+), about 1 day:
   - CheckM2 + GUNC on all 450 MAGs.
   - A multi-sample coverage screen using the bam_bins BAMs already on disk, prioritising the 35 MAGs with contamination of 10% or more, especially the two Roseovarius MePn models (19.9% and 21.4%) and the 3 betaine models.
   - Map SRR10375808 (R2_C_D2), since that sample has no local BAM.
   - This needs a new tool environment, so it is your call per CLAUDE.md.
3. In the paper, report the binned fraction per site and the assembly ceiling. Back the SF2/R2A comparisons with binning-independent gene-level data. The manuscript's IMG KO profiles already do this; an optional read-level phnJ/grdH/mcrA search is another route.
4. Ask Cliff or Susannah Tringe for Zhou's original per-sample SPAdes assemblies and the Drive bin folders. If those exist, option (b) run on them is the cleanest modernisation later.

Gate for heavier work:
- Only if reviewers insist on more recovery in restored or reference sites, run one co-assembly pilot (option c2): R2A cores, all 6 available locally. Use MEGAHIT on KBase via merged libraries, or MetaHipMer, or this machine if about 120 GB of RAM can be reserved, then multi-sample binning.
- Go further only if read recruitment in those cores rises well above about 10% and new phnJ, grdH or mcrA carriers appear.
- Full re-processing (option d) belongs in a follow-up study, preferably run on the ANL server that already holds the reads.
